Design and build a Profile Page for LYNQED — a campus-focused, location-based marketplace that connects buyers, vendors, and delivery personnel. This is a real app connected to Supabase; do not include mock JSON. Focus on UI copy, component structure, behavior, and the flows below. Use the brand tagline prominently:
“Where Buyers and Sellers Get LYNQED.”

Overall requirements (high level)

Single Profile Page /profile that adapts to every user who may have one or multiple roles: Buyer, Vendor, Delivery Personnel. Users may switch roles from profile settings. Role visibility must be conditional and straightforward.

Clean, minimal, card-based layout with expandable/collapsible sections and smooth transitions. Desktop should use a 2-column layout; on desktop move header action buttons (Cart, Orders, Profile) to top-right. Mobile stacks vertically with collapsible cards.

Currency format: Ghana cedi (prefix ₵). Use human-friendly date/time and timestamps in UTC with local timezone fallback.

Integrate with Supabase back-end tables (users, roles, vendors/stores, orders, deliveries, payouts, addresses, notifications). UI must be structured so backend endpoints can be attached later. No placeholder/mock records in the UI — use real connected data.

Copy + UI text (exact labels and button text)

Use these exact texts and labels for UI components, headings, modals and buttons.

Page header & tagline

Page title: Profile

Subtitle / tagline area: Where Buyers and Sellers Get LYNQED.

1. User Info Section (Universal - top)

Labels & fields shown:

Profile photo — displayed as avatar with overlay button: Edit photo

Full name

Email

Phone

Action buttons:

Change Password

Update Location

Edit Profile

Minimal helper text:

Under phone: Verified / Unverified badge

Under location: show human-readable address and a small Update Location CTA if missing

2. Settings Section (Universal)

Section heading: Settings

Notification Preferences — CTA: Manage notifications

Saved Addresses — CTA: Manage addresses

Privacy Settings — CTA: Privacy options

Theme Mode — toggle label: Light / Dark

Delete Account — button (danger style): Delete Account

Confirmation modal text: “Delete my account and personal data. This action cannot be undone.” Buttons: Cancel, Delete account

Logout — button: Logout

3. Role Management (Universal)

Section heading: Role & Access

Current role display: show one or many: Buyer, Vendor, Delivery Personnel (highlight the active role)

Role switch buttons (prominent):

Switch to Buyer

Switch to Vendor

Switch to Delivery Dashboard (for Delivery Personnel)

If the user is not a Delivery Personnel, show:

Register as Delivery Personnel (primary action)

Clicking opens a Registration form (see form copy below)

Registration status badge states: pending admin approval, approved, or rejected

Delivery Personnel Registration Form (modal)

Modal title: Register as Delivery Personnel
Fields & labels:

Full name (prefilled from profile)

National ID Upload — label: Upload National ID (front & back)

Profile Photo — label: Upload recent photo

Phone number

Transport Type — dropdown options: Bike, Motorbike, Car, Walking, Other

Delivery Radius (km) — number input with placeholder e.g. 5

Terms & Agreement checkbox: “I confirm my details are correct and agree to background check.”
Buttons:

Submit registration (when submitted show: “Registration submitted — status: pending admin approval.”)

Cancel

Role-specific sections (display only if that role is active)
4. Buyer Mode (only visible if active role = Buyer)

Section header: Buyer Dashboard

Dashboard Shortcut — button: Open Buyer Dashboard

Recent Orders — card list with order item summary, each item clickable to open Order Details / Tracking (see Order Tracking below)

Saved Vendors — heading + small grid/list, CTA: View vendors

Wishlist — heading + CTA: View wishlist

Delivery Preferences — small panel:

Default address: show primary address and Change link

Saved addresses: CTA: Manage addresses

Delivery instructions: editable text area with label Delivery instructions (e.g. gate code, floor) and button Save

5. Vendor Mode (only visible if active role = Vendor)

Section header: Vendor / Store Profile

Store summary card shows:

Store Name

Store Description

Store Logo (editable)

Store Location (address)

Business Hours (editable)

Pickup / Delivery Options toggles

Vendor Verification Status badge: pending / approved / rejected

Vendor management tools (CTA buttons or nav):

Manage Products

Add Product

Pending Product Approvals

Store Orders

Store Analytics

Vendor Dashboard Shortcut — button: Open Vendor Dashboard

Buttons for each area should open modals or pages that are prepared for API integration.

6. Delivery Personnel Mode (only visible if active role = Delivery Personnel)

Section header: Delivery Dashboard Summary

Status & toggle:

Online / Offline toggle (big, visible)

Key cards:

Active Deliveries — count + CTA: View

Delivery Requests — list or count + CTA

Delivery Earnings — card with Total earnings (₵) + CTA: View earnings

Delivery History — CTA: View history

Payout area:

Payment Methods — list: MoMo, Vodafone Cash, AirtelTigo, Bank with Add / Manage links

Request Payout — button: Request payout

Payout History — CTA: View payouts

Delivery Requests and Active Deliveries rows must include quick accept/reject actions and rider info for each delivery.

7. Order Tracking Logic (universal)

Order detail modal/page must show the correct flow depending on collection type.

Delivery Flow:
Order Placed → Order Received → Delivery En Route → Delivered

Pickup Flow:
Order Placed → Order Received → Order Ready for Pickup → Completed

For each stage show:

Stage name (exact text above)

Timestamp (e.g., 2025-12-07 14:32 UTC)

Status color:

Pending/earlier stages: grey

Active stage: blue/primary

Completed stage: green

Problem/failed: red

Rider contact: show rider name, phone, and Call / Message action

Visual progress bar or stepper showing current stage

Admin notes or timeline area for additions

Support CTA: Report an issue

Exact labels:

Stage label texts: Order Placed, Order Received, Delivery En Route, Delivered, Order Ready for Pickup, Completed

Progress indicator text: Progress and percent if available

Rider contact CTA: Contact rider

8. Desktop / Web View

Desktop layout: two columns. Left column for main content (User Info, Settings, Role Management, Role-specific cards). Right column for quick shortcuts: Orders, Cart, Notifications, and a compact summary card for active role.

Move header action buttons to top-right on large screens: Cart, Orders, Profile.

9. Interactions & microcopy

All major sections should be expandable/collapsible; collapsed state shows a short summary. Example collapse label: Recent Orders (3). Use smooth height transitions and fade-in for expanded content.

Use consistent card padding, subtle shadows, and 8–12px border radius for a modern look.

Buttons: primary (solid), secondary (outline), danger (red outline/solid for destructive actions).

Provide small helper/error texts for forms (e.g., “Upload a clear image of your National ID. PDF or JPG accepted.”).

For status messages and toasts use short exact copy, e.g. “Profile updated successfully.”, “Registration submitted — pending admin approval.”, “Payout request received — processing.”

Data connection & validation rules (for backend wiring)

Profile photo, national ID, and store logo must accept image uploads; validate file types jpg/png/pdf and file size limit 10MB.

Phone numbers must be validated for Ghana phone formats (allow +233 and local formats).

Role switch must set the active role value in the roles table and return permission flags for UI.

Delivery registration must set delivery_profile.status = 'pending' and create an upload record; do not allow the user to accept deliveries until status is approved.

Payout request must create a record with amount (₵), method, recipient account, and set status requested / paid / rejected.

Accessibility & UX notes

All images must have alt text.

Ensure keyboard navigability for forms and toggles.

Contrast ratios meet WCAG AA.

Use aria-labels for toggles and action buttons.

Provide explicit confirmations for destructive actions (delete account, request payout cancel).

Deliverables expected from the Studio build

High-fidelity Profile Page UI (desktop + mobile) implementing the structure above, with real data bindings to Supabase (or placeholders labeled Mapped to Supabase).

Exportable layout and component list (cards, modals, stepper, toggles, form fields), copy-ready strings, and integration notes for Supabase table mapping.

Visual states for role-switching, pending/approved/rejected badges, and order-tracking stepper states.

-- 1. Enable UUID extension for unique IDs
create extension if not exists "uuid-ossp";

-- 2. Create PROFILES table (Linked to Supabase Auth)
create table if not exists public.profiles (
  id uuid references auth.users on delete cascade primary key,
  email text,
  name text,
  avatar_url text,
  roles text[] default '{buyer}', 
  default_location text,
  phone_number text,
  is_banned boolean default false,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default timezone('utc'::text, now()) not null
);

-- 3. Create VENDORS table
create table if not exists public.vendors (
  id uuid default uuid_generate_v4() primary key,
  vendor_id text unique not null, -- e.g., 'v-123456'
  user_id uuid references public.profiles(id),
  store_name text,
  store_description text,
  store_avatar_url text,
  location text,
  contact_phone text,
  is_approved boolean default false,
  rating numeric default 5.0,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default timezone('utc'::text, now()) not null
);

-- 4. Create PRODUCTS table
create table if not exists public.products (
  id uuid default uuid_generate_v4() primary key,
  vendor_id text references public.vendors(vendor_id),
  title text,
  description text,
  price numeric,
  currency text default 'GHS',
  category text,
  images text[], -- Array of image URLs
  stock integer default 0,
  status text default 'pending', -- pending, approved, rejected
  location text,
  contact_phone text,
  rating numeric default 0,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default timezone('utc'::text, now()) not null
);

-- 5. Create DELIVERY_PERSONS table
create table if not exists public.delivery_persons (
  id uuid default uuid_generate_v4() primary key,
  user_id uuid references public.profiles(id),
  full_name text,
  vehicle_type text,
  transport_type text,
  delivery_radius integer,
  status text default 'pending', -- pending, approved, rejected, suspended
  total_deliveries integer default 0,
  rating numeric default 5.0,
  created_at timestamp with time zone default timezone('utc'::text, now()) not null
);

-- 6. Create ORDERS table
create table if not exists public.orders (
  id uuid default uuid_generate_v4() primary key,
  buyer_id uuid references public.profiles(id),
  vendor_id text,
  delivery_person_id uuid references public.profiles(id), -- Assigned driver
  items jsonb, -- Stores snapshot of items: [{productId, quantity, product: {...}}]
  total numeric,
  delivery_fee numeric default 0,
  status text default 'placed', 
  delivery_option text, -- 'delivery' or 'pickup'
  created_at timestamp with time zone default timezone('utc'::text, now()) not null
);

-- ==========================================
-- ROW LEVEL SECURITY (RLS) POLICIES
-- ==========================================

-- Enable RLS on all tables
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
alter table public.vendors enable row level security;
alter table public.products enable row level security;
alter table public.orders enable row level security;
alter table public.delivery_persons enable row level security;

-- Helper function to check if user is admin
create or replace function public.is_admin()
returns boolean as $$
select exists (
  select 1 from public.profiles
  where id = auth.uid() and 'admin' = any(roles)
);
$$ language sql security definer;

-- PROFILES Policies
create policy "Public profiles are viewable by everyone" 
  on public.profiles for select using (true);
create policy "Users can insert their own profile" 
  on public.profiles for insert with check (auth.uid() = id);
create policy "Users can update own profile" 
  on public.profiles for update using (auth.uid() = id);

-- VENDORS Policies
create policy "Vendors viewable by everyone" 
  on public.vendors for select using (true);
create policy "Users can register as vendor" 
  on public.vendors for insert with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "Owners can update vendor" 
  on public.vendors for update using (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "Admins can update vendors" 
  on public.vendors for update using (is_admin());

-- PRODUCTS Policies
create policy "Products viewable by everyone" 
  on public.products for select using (true);
create policy "Vendors can insert products" 
  on public.products for insert with check (
    exists (select 1 from public.vendors where vendor_id = products.vendor_id and user_id = auth.uid())
  );
create policy "Vendors can update own products" 
  on public.products for update using (
    exists (select 1 from public.vendors where vendor_id = products.vendor_id and user_id = auth.uid())
  );
create policy "Vendors can delete own products" 
  on public.products for delete using (
    exists (select 1 from public.vendors where vendor_id = products.vendor_id and user_id = auth.uid())
  );
create policy "Admins can update products" 
  on public.products for update using (is_admin());

-- DELIVERY_PERSONS Policies
create policy "Public view drivers" 
  on public.delivery_persons for select using (true);
create policy "Users can register as driver" 
  on public.delivery_persons for insert with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "Drivers update own" 
  on public.delivery_persons for update using (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "Admins update drivers" 
  on public.delivery_persons for update using (is_admin());

-- ORDERS Policies
-- 1. Buyers can see their own orders
create policy "Users see own orders" 
  on public.orders for select using (auth.uid() = buyer_id);
-- 2. Vendors can see orders for their shop
create policy "Vendors see orders for them" 
  on public.orders for select using (
    exists (select 1 from public.vendors where vendor_id = orders.vendor_id and user_id = auth.uid())
  );
-- 3. Drivers can see orders assigned to them OR available orders ready for pickup
create policy "Drivers see relevant orders" 
  on public.orders for select using (
    auth.uid() = delivery_person_id 
    or (status = 'ready_for_pickup' and delivery_option = 'delivery' and delivery_person_id is null)
  );
-- 4. Buyers can insert orders
create policy "Buyers can create orders" 
  on public.orders for insert with check (auth.uid() = buyer_id);
-- 5. Updates (Status changes by Vendor/Driver)
create policy "Related parties can update orders" 
  on public.orders for update using (
    auth.uid() = buyer_id 
    or exists (select 1 from public.vendors where vendor_id = orders.vendor_id and user_id = auth.uid())
    or auth.uid() = delivery_person_id
    or (status = 'ready_for_pickup' and delivery_option = 'delivery' and delivery_person_id is null) -- Allow claiming
  );

-- ==========================================
-- STORAGE BUCKETS
-- ==========================================

-- Create a storage bucket for all assets
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ('lynqed-assets', 'lynqed-assets', true)
on conflict (id) do nothing;

-- Allow public read access to storage
create policy "Public Access"
  on storage.objects for select
  using ( bucket_id = 'lynqed-assets' );

-- Allow authenticated users to upload images
create policy "Authenticated users can upload"
  on storage.objects for insert
  with check ( bucket_id = 'lynqed-assets' and auth.role() = 'authenticated' );

-- ==========================================
-- ATOMIC ORDER FUNCTION (RPC)
-- ==========================================
-- This function handles stock deduction and order creation safely

create or replace function create_order(
  p_buyer_id uuid,
  p_vendor_id text,
  p_items jsonb, -- Array of items: [{productId, quantity, ...}]
  p_total numeric,
  p_delivery_fee numeric,
  p_delivery_option text
) returns uuid as $$
declare
  item jsonb;
  prod_id uuid;
  qty int;
  current_stock int;
  new_order_id uuid;
begin
  -- 1. Loop through items to check and deduct stock
  for item in select * from jsonb_array_elements(p_items)
  loop
    prod_id := (item->>'productId')::uuid;
    qty := (item->>'quantity')::int;

    -- Lock product row for update to prevent race conditions
    select stock into current_stock
    from public.products
    where id = prod_id
    for update;

    if not found then
      raise exception 'Product % not found', prod_id;
    end if;

    if current_stock < qty then
      raise exception 'Insufficient stock for product %', prod_id;
    end if;

    -- Deduct stock
    update public.products
    set stock = stock - qty
    where id = prod_id;
  end loop;

  -- 2. Create the order
  insert into public.orders (
    buyer_id,
    vendor_id,
    items,
    total,
    delivery_fee,
    status,
    delivery_option
  ) values (
    p_buyer_id,
    p_vendor_id,
    p_items,
    p_total,
    p_delivery_fee,
    'placed',
    p_delivery_option
  ) returning id into new_order_id;

  return new_order_id;
end;
$$ language plpgsql security definer;
